title: Senior Security Engineer, AutoVM, Cloud Usage Taskforce
title_on_page: Senior Security Engineer, AutoVM, Cloud Usage Taskforce

sections.minimum_qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
- 5 years of experience with security assessments or security design reviews or threat modeling.
- 5 years of experience with security engineering, computer and network security and security protocols.
- 5 years of coding experience in one or more general purpose languages.
- 1 year of experience leading teams in a technical capacity or leading technical risk analysis in an enterprise environment.
sections.preferred_qualifications:
- Experience working with cloud tools like Terraform.
- Experience with GCP.
sections.about:
Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. Security Engineers work with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. In this role, you will also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.
The AutoVM Cloud Usage taskforce is responsible for the vulnerability management of Alphabet's GCP usage. We work on the problem by keeping Google safe from external attackers, ensuring that exploitable vulnerabilities are detected and closed quickly.
We operate across the organization, working with partner teams to ensure their cloud posture is secure while identifying vulnerabilities in all parts of the cloud stack: from virtual machine kernel bugs all the way to toxic combination of misconfigurations.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
Learn more about benefits at Google.
sections.responsibilities:
- Identify security issues and implement and design security controls, tools, and services to improve security systems and processes.
- Define the infrastructure to analyze, deploy, and manage vulnerability management across Google.
- Build a data driven approach to identify existing vulnerabilities to improve the security posture of Alphabet's use of GCP.
- Partner with other security engineers and teams to prioritize and execute on security debt reduction efforts to deliver the team's objectives and key results.
